[IRET.10.7] **Withdraw in a nested body: by identity.** A `withdraw b` in a
nested body ([LGRA.10.1.4]) cannot use a pattern position, because the rule
that runs the body is the synthetic sibling, whose activation token does not
hold `b`'s fact. It lowers instead to an `ACTION_WITHDRAW_BY_ID`, whose
`withdraw_fact_id` reads a reference to the withdrawn fact from the fact that
carries the body's captured values: the capture fact, or for a `timeout` body
its timer ([LCCO.7.2]).

- **The compiler** must add to the capture fact ([LCCO.5.2], [LTAC.3.5]) one
  slot per binding a nested body withdraws, typed by that binding's schema
  ([LGRA.5.7a.2]) and holding a reference to the fact the outer rule bound to
  it when the rule fired, and the same slot to a `timeout` clause's timer when
  its body withdraws the binding. A capture fact that carries such a slot has
  something to capture, so [LCCO.5.6] and [LTAC.3.6] do not omit it.
- **The engine** must, at fire time, resolve that reference and, when it names
  a live fact, retract that fact exactly as for `ACTION_WITHDRAW`
  ([IRET.7.8]), recorded as a `FactWithdraw` with cause `AUTHOR_WITHDRAWN`
  ([RFCS.7a.2]). A reference names one fact by its id, and an id is never
  reused ([IRET.4.4]), so once that fact has left working memory the reference
  names nothing and the action does nothing. A fact replaced by a meaningful
  change is a new fact ([LFAC.2.5.3]), so its replacement is never matched.

A runtime that does not execute this kind refuses the artefact at load
([IRET.10.6]).
